_comment: Master spec part 3: health, formal and social sciences.

source.board: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

nursing.note: Units follow the NCLEX-RN test plan's client-need categories — safe effective care, health promotion, psychosocial integrity and physiological integrity — with the foundational sciences first.

lesson.title: The Sciences Behind Nursing
lesson.summary: The body, its invaders and its medicines — the scientific core every nurse builds on.

lesson.title: Care Management, Law and Ethics
lesson.summary: Nursing as a system role — delegation, documentation and the law at the bedside.

lesson.title: Safety and Infection Control
lesson.summary: First, do no harm — precautions, the rights of medication administration and hospital-acquired conditions.

lesson.title: Health Promotion and Maintenance
lesson.summary: Keeping people well — developmental stages, screening schedules and maternal-newborn basics.

lesson.title: Psychosocial Integrity
lesson.summary: Care of the mind — communication techniques, common psychiatric conditions and crisis response.

lesson.title: Basic Care and Comfort
lesson.summary: The physiology of daily care — fluids and electrolytes, nutrition, and pressure-injury prevention.

lesson.title: Physiological Adaptation
lesson.summary: When systems fail — the major pathophysiologies and the nurse's response to them.

lesson.title: Pharmacology for Nurses
lesson.summary: Medications in practice — classes, mechanisms, monitoring parameters and dangerous interactions.

lesson.title: Risk Reduction and Diagnostics
lesson.summary: Anticipating trouble — interpreting labs and monitors and preventing complications before they land.

source.board: National Association of Boards of Pharmacy (NABP)
source.track: licensure · North American Pharmacist Licensure Examination

pharmacy.note: Units follow the NAPLEX competency areas — the foundations of pharmacotherapy, safe and accurate preparation and dispensing, and patient-centred care.

lesson.title: Pharmaceutical Sciences Foundations
lesson.summary: How drugs are built and what the body does to them — SAR, ADME and receptor theory.

lesson.title: Dosage Forms and Compounding
lesson.summary: Why form matters — tablets to infusions, dissolution, and the art of compounding.

lesson.title: Chronic Disease Pharmacotherapy
lesson.summary: The big chronic prescriptions — evidence-based regimens for the diseases most patients carry.

lesson.title: Infectious Disease and Cancer Pharmacotherapy
lesson.summary: The heavy hitters — antibiotics by mechanism, stewardship and the logic of chemo regimens.

lesson.title: Medication Safety
lesson.summary: Preventing the preventable — error taxonomy, high-alert drugs and system defences.

units.title: Interaction science and personalisation
topics: Dosing in renal and hepatic disease

lesson.title: Interactions, Genetics and Dosing
lesson.summary: Personalising therapy — CYP interactions, pharmacogenomics and organ-adjusted dosing.

lesson.title: Patient Care and Counselling
lesson.summary: The pharmacist as clinician — MTM, over-the-counter triage and vaccine practice.

units.title: Systems: law, supply and public health

lesson.title: Pharmacy Systems and Law
lesson.summary: The profession's machinery — drug law, the supply chain and pharmacy's public-health duties.

source.board: Joint Commission on National Dental Examinations (JCNDE)
source.qualification: INBDE — Integrated National Board Dental Examination
source.document: Official published examination guide and content areas
source.track: licensure · Integrated National Board Dental Examination

dentistry.note: Units follow the INBDE's content domains — the biomedical sciences through oral health and disease to clinical management — integrated the way the exam integrates them.

lesson.title: Biomedical Sciences for Dentistry
lesson.summary: The head and neck in detail — craniofacial anatomy and the physiology of the mouth.

lesson.title: Dental Biomaterials
lesson.summary: What fillings are made of — composites, ceramics and the mechanics of restorative materials.

lesson.title: Caries and Restorative Dentistry
lesson.summary: The most common disease and its repair — caries science, diagnosis and restoration.

lesson.title: Periodontology
lesson.summary: The disease of the supporting tissues — probing, classification and periodontal therapy.

lesson.title: Endodontics and Pulp Biology
lesson.summary: Inside the tooth — pulp disease, root canal therapy and dental trauma.

lesson.title: Oral Medicine and Pathology
lesson.summary: The mouth as a diagnostic window — mucosal disease, cancer and systemic connections.

lesson.title: Prosthodontics and Implants
lesson.summary: Replacing what's lost — crowns, dentures, occlusion and osseointegration.

lesson.title: Patient Management and Professional Practice
lesson.summary: Running a safe practice — anaesthesia, asepsis and the ethics of dental care.

source.qualification: NAVLE — North American Veterinary Licensing Examination

veterinary-medicine.note: Units follow the NAVLE's organisation — the veterinary sciences first, then the major species groups and the clinical disciplines that cut across them.

lesson.title: Veterinary Biomedical Sciences
lesson.summary: One medicine, many bodies — comparative physiology and the pathogens of animals.

lesson.title: Small Animal Medicine
lesson.summary: Dogs and cats — vaccination protocols, common presentations and elective surgery.

lesson.title: Equine Medicine
lesson.summary: Horses as patients — lameness workups, the colic emergency and herd health.

lesson.title: Food-Animal and Herd Medicine
lesson.summary: Medicine at herd scale — ruminants, pigs, poultry and the economics of prevention.

units.title: Veterinary surgery
topics: Principles of asepsis and tissue handling

lesson.title: Veterinary Surgery and Anaesthesia
lesson.summary: Operating across species — aseptic technique, common surgeries and multi-species anaesthesia.

lesson.title: Veterinary Diagnostics and Imaging
lesson.summary: Working up the non-verbal patient — bloods, imaging and pattern recognition.

lesson.title: One Health, Zoonoses and Food Safety
lesson.summary: Where animal and human health meet — zoonotic disease and the safety of the food chain.

lesson.title: Practice, Welfare and Ethics
lesson.summary: The profession beyond medicine — communication, economics and welfare decision-making.

source.board: Society of Actuaries (SOA) & Casualty Actuarial Society (CAS)
source.qualification: SOA/CAS Preliminary Examination syllabi (Exam P and Exam FM)

actuarial-science.note: Units follow the two gateway syllabi — Exam P's probability and Exam FM's financial mathematics — then the life-contingencies and risk-management material that follows them.

lesson.title: Probability for Actuaries
lesson.summary: The gateway syllabus — distributions, moments and the probability toolkit of risk.

lesson.title: Frequency, Severity and Compound Models
lesson.summary: Modelling claims — how often and how much, and the distributions that combine them.

lesson.title: Financial Mathematics: Interest Theory
lesson.summary: Money across time — discounting, annuities, loans and bond pricing.

lesson.title: Life Contingencies
lesson.summary: Pricing life itself — survival models and the expected values behind life insurance.

lesson.title: Ruin Theory and Reinsurance
lesson.summary: When claims outrun premiums — ruin probabilities and the reinsurance that manages them.

lesson.title: Credibility Theory
lesson.summary: Blending data and priors — how much to trust your own experience.

lesson.title: Investment and ALM Mathematics
lesson.summary: The asset side — stochastic interest, portfolio maths and matching liabilities.

lesson.title: Actuarial Practice
lesson.summary: The profession's obligations — standards, reserving regimes and explaining risk honestly.

source.qualification: EPAS — Educational Policy and Accreditation Standards

social-work.note: Units follow the EPAS structure — the profession's foundations, the nine practice competencies in sequence, and the field-education capstone.

lesson.title: The Social Work Profession
lesson.summary: What social work is and stands for — history, ethics and the generalist model.

units.title: Human behaviour and the social environment

lesson.title: Human Behaviour in the Social Environment
lesson.summary: Person-in-environment — developmental theory read through systems and structural lenses.

units.title: Diversity, equity and inclusion in practice

lesson.title: Anti-Oppressive and Culturally Humble Practice
lesson.summary: Practising with awareness of power — anti-oppressive models and cultural humility.

lesson.title: Engagement and Assessment
lesson.summary: The first moves of practice — building alliances and assessing person-in-situation.

lesson.title: Micro Practice: Individuals and Families
lesson.summary: Direct practice — casework, family systems and working a crisis safely.

lesson.title: Mezzo and Macro Practice
lesson.summary: Beyond the caseload — group work, community organising and structural change.

lesson.title: Policy Practice and Advocacy
lesson.summary: Changing the rules — welfare policy, analysis and advocacy as practice.

lesson.title: Research and Evaluation in Practice
lesson.summary: Accountable practice — evaluating programmes and reading evidence critically.

lesson.title: Field Education and Professional Self
lesson.summary: Becoming a practitioner — supervision, reflection and sustainable practice.

source.board: Council for Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs (CACREP)

counseling.note: Units follow CACREP's eight common core areas — professional counselling identity, theory, human development, relationships, group work, assessment, research and the clinical internship.

lesson.title: The Counselling Profession
lesson.summary: What counselling is and its professional spine — ethics, law and the counsellor's identity.

lesson.title: Theories of Counselling
lesson.summary: The major schools side by side — what each assumes about people and change.

lesson.title: Human Growth and Development
lesson.summary: Development as context — how growth stages shape presenting problems and treatment.

lesson.title: Helping Skills and the Alliance
lesson.summary: The craft under the theory — microskills, rapport and working across difference.

lesson.title: Group Counselling
lesson.summary: Therapy in the round — group stages, leadership styles and what makes groups heal.

lesson.title: Assessment and Diagnosis
lesson.summary: Case conceptualisation — interviews, diagnoses and the responsible use of tests.

lesson.title: Career Counselling
lesson.summary: Work as a life theme — career theories and counselling for transitions.

lesson.title: Clinical Practice and Special Populations
lesson.summary: Bringing it to the consulting room — evidence-based treatment, addictions and trauma work.

source.qualification: PAB Accreditation Document — Planning Accreditation Standards
source.document: Official published accreditation standards' curriculum requirements

urban-planning.note: Units follow PAB's required subject areas — planning history and theory, the analytic methods, the substantive planning fields, and law and practice.

units.title: Planning history and theory
topics: The evolution of cities and planning

lesson.title: Planning History and Theory
lesson.summary: Why cities are planned and by whom — a century of planning ideas and their critics.

units.title: Land use and the comprehensive plan

lesson.title: Land Use and Comprehensive Planning
lesson.summary: The plan as instrument — land-use maps, comp plans and managing growth.

lesson.title: Planning Law and Zoning
lesson.summary: The legal machinery — zoning powers, permits and the constitutional limits on planning.

lesson.title: Transportation Planning
lesson.summary: Moving a city — demand models, transit design and why new roads fill up.

lesson.title: Housing and Community Development
lesson.summary: Who lives where and why — housing economics, discriminatory history and renewal politics.

units.title: Urban design and the public realm

lesson.title: Urban Design and the Public Realm
lesson.summary: The designed city — form, walkability and what makes public space work.

lesson.title: Environmental and Resilience Planning
lesson.summary: Planning for a changing planet — adaptation, mitigation and designing for hazards.

lesson.title: Planning Methods and Analytics
lesson.summary: The analyst's toolkit — demography, GIS and scenario-building for public decisions.

source.qualification: Renfrew & Bahn — Archaeology: Theories, Methods and Practice

archaeology.note: Units follow the canonical structure — the scope of archaeology, discovery and excavation, dating and analysis, interpretation, and the world of archaeological practice today.

lesson.title: What Archaeology Is
lesson.summary: The study of the human past through what it left behind — scope, history and varieties of practice.

lesson.title: Finding the Past: Survey and Remote Sensing
lesson.summary: How sites are found without digging — geophysics, survey and imagery from the air.

lesson.title: Excavation and Stratigraphy
lesson.summary: Controlled destruction — layers, context and the discipline of the excavation record.

lesson.title: Dating Methods
lesson.summary: Putting numbers on the past — radiocarbon, tree rings and the calibration curves.

lesson.title: Artefacts, Ecofacts and Human Remains
lesson.summary: Reading objects and residues — stone tools, seeds, bones and what they say about diets and lives.

lesson.title: Interpretation: Societies, Trade and Minds
lesson.summary: From finds to societies — settlement patterns, exchange networks and ancient belief.

lesson.title: Heritage, Ethics and the Public
lesson.summary: Who owns the past — CRM, repatriation debates and archaeology's public duties.

units.title: Science and the future of archaeology

lesson.title: Archaeological Science
lesson.summary: The new microscopes on the past — aDNA, isotopes and digital reconstruction.

source.document: Published course sequence across the cognitive science core

cognitive-science.note: Units follow the interdisciplinary core as universities teach it — philosophy, psychology, neuroscience, linguistics, computation and their convergences.

lesson.title: What Is Cognitive Science?
lesson.summary: The interdisciplinary wager — minds as systems that compute over representations.

lesson.title: Perception
lesson.summary: How brains construct reality — the visual pipeline and what illusions reveal.

lesson.title: Attention and Memory
lesson.summary: The bottlenecks of thought — selective attention, memory systems and their failures.

lesson.title: Language and Cognition
lesson.summary: The human speciality — structure, meaning and how children crack the code.

lesson.title: Reasoning and Decision-Making
lesson.summary: How people actually think — heuristics, biases and the architecture of choices.

lesson.title: Cognitive Neuroscience
lesson.summary: Mapping mind to brain — imaging methods, functional systems and the hard problem.

lesson.title: Computational Models of Mind
lesson.summary: Building minds to understand them — symbolic, Bayesian and neural network models.

lesson.title: Applied Cognitive Science
lesson.summary: Cognition in the world — interface design, education and clinical applications.
